intro.heading: The short version
paragraphs: School of Gaming exists to give children a safe, fun place to learn through gaming. Protecting your family’s privacy — and your child’s most of all — matters to us, so we’ve written this in plain language instead of legal jargon.

In short: we only collect what we need to run our clubs, camps, and events. We never sell your information or your child’s. Only a parent can create a child’s account, and we never advertise to children. You can ask us to show, correct, or delete your information at any time by emailing hello@sog.gg.

whoWeAre.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: Sogverse is run by School of Gaming Galactic Oy ("School of Gaming", "we", "us"), a Finnish company. We’re responsible for looking after the personal information you and your child share with us — in legal terms, we’re the "data controller".
Here are our official details:
bullets: School of Gaming Galactic Oy (business ID 3110461-1)
Isokatu 56, 90100 Oulu, Finland
Email: hello@sog.gg

infoWeCollect.heading: The information we collect
paragraphs: We try to collect as little as possible — only what we genuinely need to run Sogverse. Here’s what that looks like:
bullets: Your name, email address, and (if you add one) phone number — so we can set up your account and keep in touch about your child’s clubs.
Your language and currency preferences — so the site shows up the way you expect.
Your password, which we store only in a scrambled (hashed) form — we can never see it.
Payment details are handled directly in Stripe. We never see or store your full card number.

About your child: their first name, their birth month and year (we don’t ask for the full date — only what we actually need), and optionally their gender — so we can place them in the right group and address them properly.
Optionally, your child’s Minecraft username — so they can connect to our Minecraft server during sessions.
Basic, anonymous information about how the site is used (see "Cookies and analytics" below).

childrensPrivacy.heading: Children’s privacy comes first
paragraphs: Most of the people using Sogverse are children, so their safety and privacy is our highest priority.

A child can never create their own account. Only a parent or guardian sets up a child’s account, chooses what to share, and gives permission on their behalf. That’s how we meet our responsibilities under data-protection law when it comes to children.

We keep children’s information to a minimum, we never show children advertising, and we never sell or share their data for marketing. During live sessions, children are always with one of our trained educators (we call them Gedus).
If you ever want to see, change, or delete your child’s information, just email hello@sog.gg and we’ll take care of it.

howWeUse.heading: How we use your information
paragraphs: We use the information above only to run Sogverse and give your family a good experience — specifically:
bullets: To create and manage your account and your child’s account.
To place your child in the right club, camp, or event group and connect them with an educator.
To run the live voice and video sessions.
To take payments and send receipts, reminders, and important updates about your clubs.
To answer your questions when you contact us for help.
To keep Sogverse safe, fix problems, and make it better over time.

legalBasis.heading: Why we’re allowed to use it
paragraphs: Data-protection law (the GDPR) asks us to have a clear reason for using your information. Ours are simple:
bullets: To deliver what you signed up for — the clubs and services you’ve bought from us (our contract with you).
Because a parent has given permission on their child’s behalf (consent).
To meet our legal duties, such as keeping accounting records for payments.
For our legitimate interest in keeping the site secure and working well — always balanced against your privacy.

providers.heading: The companies that help us run Sogverse
paragraphs: Running an online service means relying on a few trusted companies for things like hosting, payments, and email. They only handle your information to do their job for us, under contracts that require them to keep it safe. The main ones are:
bullets: Supabase — securely stores your account, family, and club information.
Stripe — processes payments. Your card details go straight to Stripe; we never see them.
Brevo — sends our emails, such as receipts and reminders.
Daily.co — powers the live voice and video sessions.
Vercel — hosts the website and provides anonymous, cookie-free usage statistics.
Meta (WhatsApp) — used to send some messages and reminders to families who prefer WhatsApp.

cookies.heading: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: We don’t use advertising or tracking cookies, and we don’t follow you around the internet.
We use a small number of necessary cookies to keep you securely logged in — the site can’t work without these, so they don’t need your consent.
To understand things like how many people visit and whether they’re using a phone or a computer, we use Vercel’s analytics. It’s privacy-friendly: no cookies, and it doesn’t identify you personally.

voice.heading: Voice and video sessions
paragraphs: Live clubs, camps, and events take place over voice and video, powered by Daily.co. Every session is led and supervised by one of our trained educators, and we use it only to deliver the session your child signed up for.

retention.heading: How long we keep your information
paragraphs: We keep your information for as long as you have an account with us. If you close your account, we delete or anonymise your information — except where the law requires us to keep certain records longer, such as Finnish accounting law, which requires payment records to be kept for several years.

storage.heading: Where your information is kept
paragraphs: Some of the companies that help us (listed above) are based outside the European Union, for example in the United States. When your information is sent to them, we make sure it’s protected by the safeguards data-protection law requires — usually the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses.

rights.heading: Your rights — and your child’s
paragraphs: You’re in control of your information. At any time you can ask us to:
bullets: Show you what information we hold about you and your child.
Correct anything that’s wrong.
Delete your information (the "right to be forgotten").
Give you a copy to take elsewhere.
Stop or limit how we use it.

security.heading: Keeping your information safe
paragraphs: We protect your information with industry-standard measures: encrypted connections, passwords stored only in scrambled form, and strict limits on who can access data. No system is ever perfectly secure, but we work hard to keep your family’s information safe.

changes.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy from time to time — for example, if we add a new feature. When we make an important change, we’ll update the date at the top and, where it matters, let you know.

contact.heading: Getting in touch and your right to complain
paragraphs: To use any of the rights above, or if you have a question about your privacy or your child’s information, just email hello@sog.gg. There’s no charge, we’ll always reply, and email is the best way to reach us.
If you’re ever unhappy with how we’ve handled your information, you have the right to complain to the Finnish Data Protection Ombudsman (Tietosuojavaltuutetun toimisto) at tietosuoja.fi.

intro.heading: The short version
paragraphs: These are the terms for using Sogverse and signing your child up for our clubs, camps, and events. We’ve written them in plain language, because we want you to actually understand what you’re agreeing to — not wade through legal jargon.

In short: our clubs happen online, with your child always supervised by a trained educator. You can cancel a monthly club whenever you like, and there’s a money-back guarantee on your child’s first session. If you ever have a question, email kanslia@sog.gg and a real person will help.

whoWeAre.heading: Who you’re agreeing with
paragraphs: Sogverse is run by School of Gaming Galactic Oy ("School of Gaming", "we", "us"), a Finnish company. These terms apply whenever you use Sogverse or buy one of our clubs, camps, or events.
Our official details:
bullets: School of Gaming Galactic Oy (business ID 3110461-1)
Isokatu 56, 90100 Oulu, Finland
Email: kanslia@sog.gg

service.heading: How our clubs work
paragraphs: Almost everything we do happens online — your child joins their club, camp, or event from home, through our website. If a particular product works differently (for example, an in-person event), we’ll always say so clearly on that product’s page before you buy.

games.heading: The games your child plays
paragraphs: Our clubs are built around video games made by other companies, such as Minecraft. We follow Finland’s official age-rating guidance.

In practice this means a child may play a game rated for up to three years above their own age, as long as a parent is present and comfortable with it — but never a game rated 18+. When you sign your child up, you’re confirming you’re happy with the age ratings of the games involved.

online.heading: Staying safe online
paragraphs: The tools we use for live sessions have their own minimum-age rules, set by the companies that make them and by local law. To keep things safe and above board, children under 13 take part using their parent’s account, and every session is supervised by one of our trained educators (we call them Gedus). Children are never online with us unsupervised.

pricing.heading: Prices and payment
paragraphs: All prices are shown in euros and include VAT. We may change our prices from time to time, but a change will never affect a club you’re already paying for without us telling you first.

clubsCancellation.heading: Cancelling a monthly club
paragraphs: Our clubs run as a monthly subscription, and you’re free to cancel whenever you like — there’s no fixed commitment. You can do it yourself from your account, and your child keeps their place until the end of the month you’ve already paid for.

We also want you to be able to try us with confidence. If your child attends their first session and it turns out not to be the right fit, let us know within 2 days of that first session and we’ll give you a full refund.

campsCancellation.heading: Cancelling a camp
paragraphs: Camps are booked and paid for as a one-off, so the cancellation terms are a little different. If you need to cancel a camp:
bullets: 14 days or more before the camp starts: you get a full refund.
Between 7 and 14 days before: we refund you minus a €50 administration fee.
Less than 7 days before: we’re unable to refund the payment, because the place has been held and prepared for your child — unless it’s a medical emergency or something genuinely outside your control.
If your child can’t attend because of illness, we’ll refund you when you send us a doctor’s certificate at kanslia@sog.gg.

conduct.heading: Behaviour and removing a child from a club
paragraphs: We want every child to feel safe and welcome, so we don’t tolerate bullying or behaviour that spoils things for others. When a problem comes up, we always start by supporting the child and helping them put it right — our full approach is set out in our <linkDiscipline>Anti-Bullying and Discipline policy</linkDiscipline>.
Only after those supportive steps, and in the case of ongoing toxic or disruptive behaviour or bullying, may we end a child’s participation. We’ll always talk it through with you first.

privacy.heading: Your family’s privacy
paragraphs: We take the privacy of your family — and your child especially — very seriously, and we handle your information in line with Finnish and EU data-protection law. Our <linkPrivacy>Privacy Policy</linkPrivacy> explains exactly what we collect and why.

changes.heading: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms from time to time, for example if we add a new kind of club or change how something works. When we make an important change, we’ll update the date at the top of this page, and where it matters we’ll let you know directly.

contact.heading: Getting in touch
paragraphs: If anything here is unclear, or you’d like to talk something through, just email kanslia@sog.gg. There’s a real person at the other end, and we’re always happy to help.

intro.heading: The short version
paragraphs: Every child should feel safe, respected, and welcome in our clubs. Bullying and unkindness have no place here, and we take them seriously.

When something goes wrong, we don’t just punish — we help. We use a calm, step-by-step approach that focuses on helping a child understand what happened, make it right, and do better next time. We only move to a firmer step if the behaviour keeps happening, and we keep you informed the whole way through.

commitment.heading: Our promise to your child
paragraphs: Our clubs are a place to learn, make friends, and have fun — and that only works if everyone feels safe. We’re committed to a community free of bullying, harassment, and cruelty, where every child is treated with respect by our educators and by each other.

approach.heading: How we handle problems
paragraphs: When a child behaves in a way that hurts or disrupts others, our educators (we call them Gedus) respond in a way that’s calm, kind, and right for the child’s age. The goal is always to help the child understand the effect of what they did and to put it right — not simply to punish.

We deal with most situations gently, with a quiet word. If the behaviour continues, we take firmer steps, one at a time. The steps below are the ladder we follow, and you’ll always be kept in the loop as we go.

step1.heading: Step 1 — A reminder and putting things right
paragraphs: The Gedu talks with your child about what happened and how it affected others, and helps them find a better way to handle it. It’s gentle and matter-of-fact — for example: "Remember not to take things from someone else’s chest without asking. You could ask them if they’d like to trade instead."

step2.heading: Step 2 — A quiet word
paragraphs: If it happens again, the Gedu has a one-on-one chat with your child to think through what they did and how it affects others. We’ll also let you know at home that we’ve talked with your child about their behaviour in the club.

step3.heading: Step 3 — Stepping in during the session
paragraphs: If the disruptive behaviour carries on, the Gedu steps in to stop it during the session — for example by muting your child for a moment or limiting what they can do in the game. The Gedu speaks with your child privately, and we message you at home.

step4.heading: Step 4 — A time-out from a session
paragraphs: If things still don’t settle, the Gedu may ask your child to sit out the rest of that session. If a longer break is needed, we’ll tell you in advance. The Gedu talks it through privately with your child, we message you at home, and our office (kanslia@sog.gg) joins the conversation.

step5.heading: Step 5 — Time away from the community
paragraphs: If the behaviour continues despite everything above, a child may be removed from the SOG community for a while — that means their clubs, our Minecraft server, and our Discord. Our office gets in touch with you to explain the decision, and we talk it through with your child too.

step6.heading: Step 6 — A fresh start later
paragraphs: Time away isn’t necessarily the end. Your child can come back when you and they both feel ready for it. If they return and the behaviour hasn’t changed, we’ll step them out of the activity for good rather than starting the ladder over — but our hope, always, is a fresh start that works.

partnership.heading: We’re in this together
paragraphs: You know your child best, and we get the best results when we work together. If you have any worries about how your child is getting on — or if you think they’re being treated unkindly by someone else — please tell us. Sharing the same expectations at home and in the club makes a real difference.

contact.heading: Getting in touch
paragraphs: If you have any questions about this policy, or you’d like to talk about something that’s happened, email our office at kanslia@sog.gg. There’s a real person at the other end, and we’re here to help.

robloxPrivacy.title: Roblox Programme Privacy Policy
robloxPrivacy.subtitle: For families registering for the youth digital creativity Programme in France delivered by Lynx Educate and School of Gaming and sponsored by Roblox.

intro.heading: The short version — for parents and young people
blocks: The Programme is for young people in France aged 8–17. A parent or legal guardian must complete registration.

We collect only what we need to register your child, deliver the Programme safely and understand whether it is working. This includes the parent’s contact details, limited information about the child, the child’s Roblox username or User ID, and information about attendance, completion and game publication.

School of Gaming uses information to operate the registration and learning platform. Lynx Educate processes Programme information as needed to manage delivery. Each organisation has different responsibilities depending on the activity and the purpose for which personal information is used.
School of Gaming is the data controller for the operation of Sogverse and the personal information it processes for its own platform services.

For the limited Programme impact research carried out on behalf of Roblox, Roblox is the data controller, Lynx Educate acts as Roblox’s data processor, and School of Gaming acts as Lynx Educate’s approved sub-processor.

Where Lynx Educate processes personal information for its own independently determined purposes (such as optional Lynx email communications), Lynx Educate acts as the data controller for that processing.
The following choices are optional and will not affect your child’s place:
Emails to the parent from Lynx Educate about future Roblox events and gaming resources.
Photography or filming for private Programme reporting to Roblox.
Public use of photographs or footage by Lynx Educate, School of Gaming and Roblox.
Routine online sessions are not recorded. A child will not be photographed or filmed where the required permission has not been given or where the child does not want to take part.
Lynx Educate and School of Gaming do not sell Programme registration information or use it to advertise to children.
You and your child may ask to see, correct or delete information, withdraw an optional consent, or object to certain uses by contacting support@lynxeducate.com or hello@sog.gg.

applies.heading: Who this policy applies to
blocks: This policy applies to parents, legal guardians and young people registering for the Roblox youth digital creativity Programme in France (The Programme).
The Programme is for young people aged 8–17. A parent or legal guardian must complete registration and confirm that they have authority to register the child.

The policy covers Programme registration, administration, learning sessions, events, support, safeguarding and impact evaluation. It supplements School of Gaming’s <linkPrivacy>general Privacy Policy</linkPrivacy>. Where the two policies conflict in relation to this Programme, this Programme-specific policy applies.
The child’s separate use of a Roblox account, Roblox Studio or another Roblox service is governed by Roblox’s own privacy policy and terms.
The <linkRobloxTerms>Programme Terms</linkRobloxTerms> establish the 8–17 age range, parent-led registration and Programme-specific data sharing.

responsible.heading: Who is responsible for the information

responsibleLynx.heading: Lynx Educate SAS
blocks: Lynx Educate manages learner recruitment, Programme administration, operational delivery, participant communications and reporting.
Lynx Educate SAS
185 rue Ordener
75018 Paris, France
Email: support@lynxeducate.com

blocks: School of Gaming operates Sogverse, manages the registration and learning environment, provides the curriculum and facilitators, delivers learning sessions and ensures safeguarding oversight.
School of Gaming Galactic Oy

Isokatu 56

responsibleRoblox.heading: Roblox Corporation
blocks: Roblox sponsors the Programme and operates the Roblox platform.
Roblox is a separate data controller for:
Information processed through the child’s Roblox account or use of Roblox Studio.
The limited Programme dataset Roblox receives for its internal Programme-impact research.
Photographs, footage or related material supplied to Roblox under an optional media permission.

collectParent.heading: About the parent or guardian
blocks: We may collect:
Name and email address.
Telephone number, where provided.
Preferred language and communication preferences.
Sogverse account and login information. Passwords are stored in hashed form and cannot be read by staff.
Confirmation of acceptance of the <linkRobloxTerms>Programme Terms</linkRobloxTerms> and this Privacy Policy.
Privacy acknowledgements and optional consent choices.
Messages, support requests, complaints and safeguarding communications.
Attendance at parent sessions and optional survey responses.
The Programme is free, so no payment-card information is required for Programme participation.

collectChild.heading: About the child
blocks: Depending on the activity, we may collect:
A display name and, where genuinely needed, a first name.
Age, age bracket, or birth month and year rather than a full date of birth.
Roblox username and Roblox User ID.
The course, club, camp, event or group attended.
Attendance, participation, learning progress and completion.
Whether the child publishes their first Roblox game, experience or digital item.
The name or link of a published experience where required to verify the Programme outcome.
Learner feedback and optional survey responses.
Limited moderation, behavioural or safeguarding information where needed to keep participants safe.
Accessibility, dietary or health information provided for a particular event, but only where necessary.
Photographs, footage, audio or related media where the relevant optional permission has been given.
We do not ask for the child’s Roblox password. The child does not need to provide a separate email address for Sogverse where the account is managed through the parent or guardian.

collectTechnical.heading: Technical information
blocks: Sogverse may process limited technical information required to operate and secure the service, including:
Login and security records.
Browser, device and operating-system information.
IP address and error information.
Necessary session cookies.
Basic website-usage statistics.

These categories reflect SOG’s <linkPrivacy>generic Privacy Policy</linkPrivacy>, its privacy-first Sogverse architecture and the Programme’s attendance, completion and publication reporting requirements.

use.heading: How and why we use the information

useDeliver.heading: To register and deliver the Programme
blocks: We use account, age, enrolment and contact information to:
Confirm eligibility.
Create and manage the family’s Sogverse profile.
Place the child in an appropriate group.
Schedule and deliver online or in-person activities.
Provide learning support and important Programme communications.
Help the child build and publish a Roblox experience.
This processing is necessary to provide the Programme under the Terms accepted by the parent or guardian and for our legitimate interests in delivering a safe and effective educational service.

useSafety.heading: To keep children and the service safe
blocks: We use limited account, session, moderation and incident information to:
Protect accounts and prevent unauthorised access.
Supervise sessions and respond to inappropriate behaviour.
Investigate complaints and safeguarding concerns.
Communicate with a parent or guardian.
Contact emergency services or competent authorities where necessary.
Protect the rights, safety and welfare of participants, facilitators and other people.
We rely on our legitimate interests in operating a safe Programme, applicable legal obligations and, in an emergency, the protection of someone’s vital interests.

useEvaluate.heading: To evaluate the Programme
blocks: We use attendance, completion, publication outcomes, parent participation and survey information to understand whether the Programme is achieving its objectives and to prepare Programme reports.
Where possible, reports use aggregated or anonymised information that does not identify an individual child.
This processing is based on the legitimate interests of the organisations involved in evaluating and improving the Programme, balanced against the enhanced protection owed to children.

useEmail.heading: Optional email communications
blocks: Lynx Educate uses the parent’s email address to send information about future Roblox events and gaming resources only where the parent selects the optional email checkbox.
This use is based on the parent’s consent. It is not required for participation and can be stopped through the unsubscribe link in any email or by contacting Lynx Educate.
School of Gaming and Roblox do not receive the parent’s email under this checkbox for their own marketing.

useMedia.heading: Optional photography and filming
blocks: Photography, filming and public communications are based on separate, optional permissions. Declining either media option will not affect registration or participation.
Consent is not the legal basis for the core registration, delivery or safeguarding activities described above.

research.heading: Limited information shared with Roblox for impact research
blocks: Under the Programme’s current Data Processing Addendum, the identifiable information that may be provided to Roblox for internal impact research is limited to:
Roblox username.
Roblox User ID.
The email address associated with the Programme account, which may be the parent or guardian’s email.
The particular Programme service or activity attended.
Roblox uses this dataset for internal research into the benefits and impact of the Programme. It is not supplied through the Programme for advertising or direct marketing.
Roblox may also receive aggregated attendance, completion, publication and satisfaction reporting that does not identify individual families.

The optional photography and marketing choices do not control this limited research transfer. The transfer is explained through the Privacy Policy and acknowledged through the required registration checkbox.
Parents and participants may object to this processing by contacting Lynx Educate or School of Gaming, and the request will be passed to Roblox for assessment.

marketing.heading: Email marketing from Lynx Educate
blocks: Where the parent selects the optional email box:
Only the parent’s email address is used.
Emails are sent by Lynx Educate.
The emails relate to future educational events and gaming resources.
The parent can unsubscribe at any time.
Declining or withdrawing consent does not affect the child’s Programme participation.

Lynx Educate keeps the marketing contact information until the parent unsubscribes or, where there has been no interaction, for no more than three years from the last contact. A minimal suppression record may then be retained to ensure the parent is not added back to the mailing list.

media.heading: Photography, filming and public use
blocks: Routine online sessions are not recorded. Where photography or filming is planned for a selected session or event, families will be told in advance.
There are two separate optional choices.

mediaSponsor.heading: Private sponsor reporting
blocks: The first media choice permits the child to be photographed or filmed for private Programme reporting to Roblox as Programme sponsor. This may include internal impact reports, delivery updates or sponsor presentations.
This permission does not permit publication on websites, social media or in the press.

mediaPublic.heading: Public impact communications
blocks: The second media choice permits Lynx Educate, School of Gaming and Roblox to use photographs or footage publicly to show the impact of the Programme, including on:
Their websites.
Their social-media channels.
Press and public-relations materials.
Programme and impact communications.
Public content may be accessible worldwide and may be copied or shared by other users beyond the organisations’ control.

mediaChildAgrees.heading: The child must also agree
blocks: The parent should discuss the media choice with the child before selecting it. We will also explain the photography or filming to the child in an age-appropriate way.

We will not deliberately photograph or film a child who objects, even where a parent previously selected a media checkbox. Staff will use reasonable practical measures to keep children without permission out of identifiable footage.

mediaCaseStudies.heading: Case studies, names and participant-created content
blocks: The two registration media boxes cover photographs and footage only.
A separate written release will be obtained before using:
A child’s full name.
A named or detailed case study.
A testimonial or quotation.
An audio interview.
Identifiable survey responses.
Game screenshots linked to the child.
Participant-created content or intellectual property.

mediaChanging.heading: Changing a media choice
blocks: A parent or child may withdraw a media permission by contacting us or using the available Sogverse setting.

After withdrawal, we will stop new uses and remove material from channels we control where reasonably possible. Withdrawal cannot make earlier lawful use unlawful, undo printed materials already distributed, or guarantee deletion of copies already shared by third parties.

childSafety.heading: Children’s privacy and safety
blocks: The Programme uses a private and moderated learning environment.
Every child’s profile is linked to a parent or guardian account.
Children use a display name rather than publishing their contact details.
Only registered participants and vetted facilitators may join.
Communication is group-based and supervised.
There is no private direct messaging between children.
Routine sessions are not recorded.
Lynx Educate and School of Gaming do not use Programme registration data for behavioural advertising to children.

Safeguarding concerns are handled under the joint <linkRobloxSafeguarding>Child Safeguarding Policy</linkRobloxSafeguarding>. School of Gaming handles day-to-day concerns in the first instance and escalates serious matters to Lynx Educate. Emergency services are contacted first where a child may be in immediate danger.

Children must also receive an age-appropriate explanation of how their information is used. French law requires information addressed to a child to be clear and easily understandable. Where an online processing activity genuinely relies on consent and concerns a child under 15, French law requires the child and the holder or holders of parental authority to consent jointly.

helpers.heading: Who else helps us deliver the Programme
blocks: Information may be accessed only where necessary by:
Authorised Lynx Educate personnel.
Authorised School of Gaming personnel and trained Game Educators.
Roblox for the limited research and consented media uses described above.
Event venues, accessibility providers or photographers that need limited information for a particular activity.
Professional advisers, insurers, emergency services, safeguarding bodies or public authorities where required.
Technical providers that operate Sogverse.
School of Gaming’s principal technical providers currently include:
Supabase, for account and Programme information.
Brevo, for operational emails and reminders.
Daily.co, for live voice and video functionality.
Vercel, for website hosting and privacy-friendly analytics.
Meta/WhatsApp, only where a family chooses WhatsApp communications.
These providers may process information only to perform their contracted services and must protect it appropriately.

transfers.heading: International transfers
blocks: Lynx Educate is based in France and School of Gaming is based in Finland.
Roblox is based in the United States, and some technical providers may also process information outside the European Economic Area.

Where information is transferred outside the EEA, the responsible organisation uses an approved transfer mechanism, such as an adequacy decision or the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses, together with appropriate security measures.
The Roblox–Lynx Data Processing Addendum includes Standard Contractual Clauses and requirements concerning encryption, pseudonymisation, access control, logging, separation and secure deletion.

retention.heading: How long we keep information
blocks: We do not keep every type of information for the same period.
Sogverse account information: kept while the family account is active and then deleted or anonymised, except where a limited record must lawfully be retained.
Programme administration and participation information: kept until Programme delivery, final reporting and reasonable follow-up are complete, then deleted or anonymised.
Roblox research dataset: returned or securely deleted when the relevant processing services end, unless applicable law requires limited retention.
Marketing information: kept until the parent unsubscribes.
Media and media permissions: kept for the permitted reporting or publication purpose and reviewed periodically.
Safeguarding, incident and legal records: may be kept longer where necessary to protect a child, investigate a concern, comply with law, or establish or defend legal claims.
Security records: kept only for the period reasonably needed to protect and investigate the service.
Closing a Sogverse account does not automatically close a separate Roblox account or remove an experience published on Roblox.

rights.heading: Your rights — and your child’s rights
blocks: Depending on the circumstances, the parent and child may ask us to:
Provide access to the personal information held.
Correct inaccurate or incomplete information.
Delete information.
Restrict how information is used.
Provide certain information in a portable format.
Object to processing based on legitimate interests, including identifiable Programme-impact research.
Withdraw an optional consent at any time.
Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that was lawful before withdrawal.
Children may contact us directly about their own information. Parents or legal guardians may also make a request for a child, subject to the child’s own rights, age and maturity.
There is no solely automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects on participants.
Send requests to support@lynxeducate.com or hello@sog.gg. The organisations will coordinate the response and route Roblox-related requests to Roblox where necessary.
Families also have the right to complain to the Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés — CNIL.

security.heading: Keeping information safe
blocks: We use measures appropriate to the risks involved, including:
Encryption in transit and at rest.
Hashed passwords.
Role-based access controls.
Access and security logging.
Pseudonymisation where appropriate.
Logical separation of datasets.
Backups and incident-response procedures.
Confidentiality obligations for personnel and contractors.
Restrictions on downloading, copying and reusing participant information.

robloxSafeguarding.title: Roblox Programme Child Safeguarding Policy
robloxSafeguarding.subtitle: This sits alongside School of Gaming’s <linkDiscipline>Anti-Bullying policy</linkDiscipline>, which continues to apply to day-to-day behaviour in sessions. This document covers Lynx Educate and School of Gaming’s broader safeguarding responsibilities for the Programme, including in-person events.
robloxSafeguarding.pendingContact: A School of Gaming contact address for safeguarding concerns is still being confirmed and will be added here.

intro.heading: Our commitment
blocks: Every child taking part in this Programme has the right to feel safe, respected and protected — whether they’re joining online or attending an in-person event. Lynx Educate and School of Gaming both take this responsibility seriously.

covers.heading: Who this covers
blocks: This policy applies to all Lynx Educate and School of Gaming staff, facilitators (Game Educators, or “Gedus”), volunteers, and any contractor who interacts with children through this Programme.

vetting.heading: Before someone works with children
blocks: All Game Educators (Gedus) are required to complete School of Gaming’s own vetting and training process before working with children on Sogverse. This includes:

online.heading: During online sessions
blocks: Every Gamer’s account is linked to a parent account; children cannot register themselves.
There is no direct messaging between children — all communication is group-based and actively supervised by a trained Game Educator.
Only registered Gamers and vetted Educators can take part — no external invites or outside contacts.
Sessions are not recorded.

behaviour.heading: Behaviour and discipline
blocks: Day-to-day behavioural issues during SOG-delivered sessions follow School of Gaming’s <linkDiscipline>Anti-Bullying and Discipline policy</linkDiscipline>, which uses a supportive, step-by-step approach before any child is removed from a session or the community.

escalation.heading: Escalation protocol
blocks: Concerns are handled by School of Gaming in the first instance, given day-to-day contact with participants. Any safeguarding concern — abuse, harassment, self-harm, or serious injury — is escalated to Lynx Educate within 24 hours, and Lynx will inform Roblox promptly where required. Where a child may be at immediate risk, we contact emergency services first, before any internal escalation.

concern.heading: If you have a concern
blocks: If you or your child have a safeguarding concern, please contact support@lynxeducate.com.

data.heading: Data and photos
blocks: Any photography, filming, or use of a child’s image is governed by the consent choices set out in the <linkRobloxPrivacy>Roblox Programme Privacy Policy</linkRobloxPrivacy> — never assumed, always optional, always changeable.

review.heading: Reviewing this policy
blocks: We review this policy annually.

intro.heading: The short version
blocks: This explains what you’re signing your child up for when you register for the Roblox Programme. It’s a joint programme between Lynx Educate and School of Gaming, sponsored by Roblox. If anything’s unclear, email support@lynxeducate.com.

involved.heading: Who’s involved
blocks: Lynx Educate SAS and School of Gaming Galactic Oy (“SOG”) design and deliver this Programme together — in this document, “we”/“us” means both of us jointly, unless we say otherwise.
Roblox Corporation (“Roblox”) sponsors the Programme and provides the platform your child will build on. Roblox is not a party to these Terms.

Registration and sessions happen on School of Gaming’s platform (“Sogverse”). By registering, you’re agreeing to these Programme-specific terms, which apply alongside (and take precedence over, where they conflict with) <linkTerms>School of Gaming</linkTerms> and Lynx’s standard Terms and Conditions.

eligibility.heading: Who can take part
blocks: The Programme is for young people in France, aged 8–17, registered by a parent or legal guardian. A parent or guardian must complete registration and consent on the child’s behalf.

whatsInvolved.heading: What’s involved
blocks: Your child will take part in sessions (online and/or in-person, depending on what you’ve registered for) designed to teach game-building skills on the Roblox platform, culminating in publishing their own game or item. Parents are invited to separate sessions on online safety and parental controls.

cost.heading: Cost
blocks: The Programme is free to registered families.

safety.heading: Safety and supervision
blocks: Every session is supervised by a trained facilitator. Our approach to behaviour and safeguarding is set out in our joint <linkRobloxSafeguarding>Child Safeguarding Policy</linkRobloxSafeguarding>, available upon request.

information.heading: Your information
blocks: How we use your and your child’s information is explained in our <linkRobloxPrivacy>Roblox Programme Privacy Policy</linkRobloxPrivacy>. By registering, you confirm you’ve read and understood it.

When enrolling in a Roblox programme, the information associated with your School of Gaming account (including your contact details and your child’s account information) will also be shared with Lynx Educate for the purposes of delivering the programme and with Roblox for the purposes of programme impact research.

media.heading: Photos, video, and marketing
blocks: Whether your child is photographed or filmed, and whether that’s used for marketing, depends entirely on the choices you make at registration. These are optional and you can change your mind at any time in your Sogverse profile settings.

concern.heading: If you have a concern
blocks: If you’re concerned about your child’s experience in the Programme, contact support@lynxeducate.com — we’ll make sure it reaches the right people.

changes.heading: Changes to these terms
blocks: We may update these terms; we’ll always update the date above and tell you directly if something important changes.

attributions.title: Attributions

entries.laPoste: The French postal codes in that same list, so a family in France can type their code instead of hunting for their commune.
